  1. Check out Fall and Winter Programs

    The Waukee Parks and Recreation Department have a ton of fall and winter programs, activities and events planned for you! Check out the online program guide to find your favorite. Registration opens September 1, but a few programs are already open! Read on...

  2. Things to Know for Post Storm Clean-up

    If you are cleaning up after recent storms and have yard debris or household materials to throw out, read this guidance for curbside pick-up. Do not put household hazardous waste on the curb or in your trash bins. Take that to the Metro Waste facility. Read on...

  3. Things to Do for August and September

    Last call for the Healthy Lawn Program or the Economic Development Bus Tour plus more fun options to round out your summer and get a delightful start to fall! Read on...

  4. What and Where Can You Ride in Waukee?

    With the goal of making travel safer in Waukee, the Waukee City Council approved a new personal transportation device ordinance on July 20 to establish clearer rules for scooters, bicycles, e-bikes, e-motos and other personal transportation devices. Read on...

  5. Road Work in Waukee

    See current lane, street and trail closures as well as work on traffic signals within Waukee city limits. Read on...

  1. Add an Event!

    Community organizations are welcome to submit events to the Community Calendar. The City encourages submission of events which cater to the whole community, such as pancake breakfasts, free concerts, ribbon cuttings and so on.
